axes: +X face right, +Y face up, +Z toward crew

mounting.placement: identity child of existing slot; apply slot pose exactly once
mounting.source_aspect: square face from original AOH schematic; absolute dimensions provisional
mounting.decision: fit 61mm square into 140x65mm provisional slot, no anisotropic scaling; coordinator must retain neutral backing around unfilled area
mounting.dimension_confidence: provisional, not surveyed LM5 or mechanically qualified

supported_mode.source: simulation truth converted by LM into lunar-surface yaw frame; not measured radar, AGC error-counter output or AGS
supported_mode.saturation: clamp finite normalized display value to [-1,+1]
supported_mode.phase: descent only; reject ascent, abort and rendezvous
supported_mode.frame: surface-relative horizontal velocity resolved into yaw heading forward/right; radial velocity excluded
supported_mode.polarity_qualification: operational inference from ZERLINA50 fly-to statement, not verified Apollo11 wiring
supported_mode.positive_forward: horizontal bar moves UP (+local Y), suggesting pitch back to reduce forward speed
supported_mode.positive_right: vertical bar moves LEFT (-local X), suggesting roll left to reduce rightward speed
sources: AOH table3-1 p3-16 and X-POINTER SCALE entry

needles.mechanical_fidelity: independently translated shallow curved visual blades; internal rotary mechanism and pivot geometry not surveyed

scale.multiplier_state: both inactive for LO MULT velocity; HI and LOS not runtime supported

invalid_data.action: hide /CrossPointer/Needles; do not center invalid values or show false zero
invalid_data.policy_origin: explicit application policy, not modeled meter electrical failure

forbidden_runtime_assumptions: no inferred input gesture or collider
no claim that body velocity equals horizontal at large attitude

presentation.historical_face: only source-backed FWD VEL/LAT VEL and multiplier legends; no synthetic source/mode placard
presentation.source_qualification: interface and handoff; optional host training UI, not production spacecraft ink
